chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

If you intend to depart on one of the two days, you are not permitted to depart until the sun passes its zenith; and if you delay until the last of the days of Tashriq, which is the final day of departure, there is no blame upon you regardless of what time you depart and throw [the pebbles], before or after the zenith.

key_terms.التَّشْرِيق: The days of Eid following the Day of Sacrifice, specifically the 11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah
key_terms.الزَّوَال: The time of solar noon, when the sun begins to decline from its highest point
key_terms.تَزُولَ الشَّمْسُ: The passing of the sun from its zenith (solar noon)
key_terms.يَوْمُ النَّفْرِ الْآخِرِ: The final day of departure (13th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific time restrictions for leaving Mina during the days of Tashriq in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani’s chain in al-Istibsar clarifies the juristic distinction between the first two days of Eid al-Adha and the final day of Tashriq regarding the timing of Nafar from Mina. It establishes that while early departure is prohibited before solar noon on the initial days to ensure full participation in rituals, the final day offers flexibility, reflecting the Shia emphasis on ease (rukhas) in the concluding rites of Hajj.
